who: People working in a second language
takeaways: If you set a time limit, people can turn it off, adjust it to at least ten times the default, or extend it.
To extend, people are warned before time runs out, get at least 20 seconds to extend with a simple action such as one button, and can do it at least ten times.
Some people need far longer to read, type or move through a screen. A limit that feels generous to you can lock them out.
Exceptions: real-time events like auctions, limits that are essential to the activity, and limits longer than 20 hours.
failures: A session that expires with no warning, losing the form
A timed checkout with no way to ask for more time
A toast with an Undo button that vanishes before people can reach it
check: List every timer in the flow, visible or not: sessions, holds, toasts, auto-advancing steps.
For each one, find how people turn it off, adjust it or extend it.
Check the warning gives at least 20 seconds and that extending is a single, simple action.

quiz.question: A banking app signs people out after 10 minutes of inactivity. What is the simplest way to meet 2.2.1?
options: Show a countdown in the header so people can see it
Warn before time runs out, with a “Stay signed in” button and at least 20 seconds to press it
quiz.why: A visible countdown still ends with no choice, and a longer fixed limit is still a fixed limit. A warning with a one-press extend lets anyone take the time they need.

spec: List each time limit, its length, and whether it can be turned off, adjusted or extended.
Design the warning dialog: when it appears, its wording, and the extend button.
Note what happens when time does run out, and what data is kept.
review: Where in this flow can time run out on someone?
Who decided this limit, and what is it protecting?
If someone is twice as slow as you, what happens?
tradeoff: Security and stock teams want short limits. Keep the limit, but always warn and let people extend it with one action. That keeps the protection without punishing slow users.
system: Provide one timeout warning pattern in the library, with the warning time and extend action built in.
pitch: Every surprise timeout is a lost form and a frustrated customer. A warning with one button keeps them, and keeps the security.
